scenarios.name: wire-payload-accounting

checks.name: payload-contract-present

checks.name: manifest-entries-present

scenarios.name: degraded-transport-contract

checks.name: inline-schema-parses
checks.detail: the in-message schema is valid JSON object form

checks.name: inline-schema-carries-full-contract
checks.detail: inline schema top-level required/properties match the real model schema

checks.name: inline-schema-keeps-nested-definitions
checks.detail: nested $defs survive (degraded modes lose the tools[] copy entirely)

notes: Schema dedup MUST be mode-conditional: when the adapter falls back to json-object/plain, this in-message contract is the only schema the model sees. Removing it unconditionally would remove the contract exactly when tool enforcement is weakest.

scenarios.name: quota-fail-fast

checks.detail: strict wire body keeps the in-message response_schema contract

checks.name: degraded-json-object-keeps-contract
checks.detail: json-object wire body keeps the in-message response_schema contract

checks.name: degraded-plain-keeps-contract
checks.detail: plain wire body keeps the in-message response_schema contract

checks.name: tool-call-wire-has-schema-once
checks.detail: tool-call wire body carries the schema only in tools[].function

checks.name: request-size-keeps-packing-headroom
checks.detail: packing measure (request_size) stays unstripped and the stripped tool-call wire is strictly smaller, so no degraded re-send can overflow a budget its tool-call send fit in; the strict-mode response_format block is a pre-existing overhead request_size never included (tool-call wire 5,275 B vs unstripped 11,036 B, saved 5,761 B)

notes: Strip is adapter-side and mode-conditional by construction: providers keep emitting the inline contract (scenario 2), so degraded modes and codex transport are unchanged. Only tool-call bodies lose the duplicate.

checks.name: authorized-contraction-publishes
checks.detail: attempt 2 replayed as accepted with 1 published finding(s)

checks.name: authorized-contraction-is-resolution-backed
checks.detail: 6 candidate evidence IDs contracted, all cited by an adjudicator resolution (0 unauthorized)

checks.name: unauthorized-contraction-rejected
checks.detail: attempt 3 replayed as rejected with 0 published finding(s)

checks.name: heuristic-only-claim-not-published
checks.detail: attempt 1 replayed as rejected; the candidate rests on 4 model-estimate metrics while the run records verified completion and zero wrong actions

checks.name: identical-duplicate-objections-collapse
checks.detail: 2 identical duplicate objection ID(s) in the recorded auditor response collapse to one each and adjudication proceeds

checks.name: recorded-duplicate-shape-is-real
checks.detail: the replayed duplicate objections are byte-identical, so collapsing them cannot hide a disagreement

checks.name: accepted-baseline-still-publishes
checks.detail: attempt 5 replayed as accepted with 1 published finding(s)

notes: These five checks are the definition of 'did not worsen quality'. Any prompt change, gate change, or payload reshaping must keep the authorized contraction publishing, the unauthorized one rejecting, the heuristic-only claim unpublished, the duplicates collapsed, and the accepted baseline finding published.

scenarios.name: prompt-prefix-stability

checks.name: static-blocks-serialize-first
checks.detail: payload key order is ['corpus_manifest', 'response_schema', 'ux_principle_pack', 'role_input', 'evidence_request_policy', 'resolved_evidence']

checks.name: rounds-share-the-static-prefix
checks.detail: consecutive analyst rounds share 25,535 of 26,048 payload bytes; the static prefix is 25,455 bytes

notes: Provider prompt caching only reuses a request prefix, so the reusable bytes must come first. Alphabetical key order put the 17 kB principle pack and 5 kB response schema behind the 0.5 kB per-round retrieval policy, which truncated the reusable prefix to the 2.8 kB corpus manifest and held the observed cache hit ratio to 0.3-13% across 1.38M prompt tokens on one identical corpus. Reordering is serialization-only: key names, values, and the system prompt are unchanged, so no prompt_version bump is due.
